subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Dying and Rising Gods
description: A micro-lesson that makes Dying and Rising Gods usable.

hook.text: Osiris, Tammuz, Adonis, Attis, Persephone—gods die and return across cultures. The pattern is everywhere.

buildup.text: James Frazer linked dying gods to agricultural cycles. They die at harvest and return in spring.

discovery.text: Frazer's book The Golden Bough argued myths encode farming knowledge. Death and growth share one story.

twist.text: Modern scholars question universal links. Each myth has its own context. Pattern-matching can overreach.

climax.text: Whether connected or not, the dying-rising pattern shows a universal human need: death must not be final.

punchline.text: Gods die and return because we need them to.

quiz.question: Who wrote The Golden Bough about dying and rising gods?
